slots.why: DUNGEONS.md section 1: 4 slots per dungeon, one strip each, 2,048 long in x and at most 64 wide in z, 128-block rows from z 1,024. Slot k of dungeon d is row (d-1)*4 + (k-1): its strip is z0 = rows_from_z + row * row_spacing .. z0 + strip_width_max - 1, x origin_x .. origin_x + strip_length - 1, its spine along +x at the strip's centre line z0 + strip_width_max / 2. tools/dungeon.py refuses any overlap with the portals' rescue box (z -512..768 on every x), Entei's band (z around -768) and the probe pack's row (z -704..-577, data/dungeon_probes.json), each recomputed from its own file
slots.overworld_coincidence: the rows are inside the overworld map's x/z bounds (data/world.json 0..8191), unlike Entei's (data/entei_boss.json pocket.origin_why). What that risks is the blackout's waystone arrival test, which compares coordinates and not dimensions (data/blackout.json checkpoints.waystone_jump_why): tools/dungeon.py refuses any slot's arrival point within waystone_arrival_radius + 1 of a town waystone in data/progression.json, and the keeper's own box tests are made dimension-safe by the dg.pk tag (a box test on @s is coordinate-only)
slots.clear_strip_why: false for the placeholder: the pocket is void, so the shell writes only its own boxes. A shell from an earlier, LONGER spine is not cleared by a later shorter one; set true for the first apply of the real spine (step 4) to air the whole strip first (I2, EXP-081: one 2,048 x 64 strip cleared in one function call stalls the server 2.64 s fresh). A re-apply step only, never at entry

draw.rule: A rip click (door/rip_<name>) runs `draw` as the player: band from the RCT cap (m/band); candidates are the dungeons whose first_band is at or under the band and whose gate_flag is held (the playtest tag bypasses a gate), not locked out, with a free slot; the one drawn least recently wins, a random number breaks a tie; that dungeon's own door/<short> then runs unchanged (its checks, then the sigil last). The stamp is taken at the go, so a refusal never counts and a back-out does (no re-roll). Nothing in the keeper.
draw.tiers: tier 1 = band, gate, lockout and a free slot; tier 2 (only when tier 1 is empty) = band and gate alone, so the dungeon's own door refuses with its lockout or busy message and takes nothing. No eligible dungeon at all (cap unread, band 0): the first dungeon's door refuses.
draw.age: dg.dr_<short> holds #up at the last go; a never-drawn dungeon, or a stamp ahead of #up, is the oldest (2147483000). The ties for the oldest are broken by `random value 0..1073741823` taken mod the count (a bias of 1 in 2^30 per tie).
draw.way_out: dg.rip, set at the go from the rip clicked, is where m/out leads; a player with no dg.rip (a run begun before the rips were separate, or a score never set) leaves by the first rip in data/dungeon_rips.json. The 13 rips that once stood for the dungeons on the old mine's trail were retired 2026-10-13, so no rip stands for a dungeon any more.

Candies (153 cp); band 4 lost one Lum Berry (193 -> 185 cp, under the 188 cp limit); band 6 is one Super Potion, 3 Potions and 3 XL Exp. Candies for two Super Potions and 2 candies (352 cp, over the 348 cp limit). dungeons.design: Pass 3 (unit DG3-JUNGLE, 2026-10-10), after the owner's walk of pass 2 ('I see no diverging paths ... the optional paths didn't feel immense. And the parkour room should be longer'), on pass 2's rooms. The OUTER JUNGLE: the strangler thicket (maze), the troop's clearing (nest), north and up the root stair, the canopy crossing (the main parkour, six sections). The GORGE RIM is a three-way crossroads, every way in sight from its middle: the poachers' trail east (dark, a fight: the camp, with the cracked secret), the rope bridge north (sunlit, fast, a collapse that costs a fall) or the flooded stair south into the gorge (safe and long); all three meet in the wild orchard (resources). The TEMPLE: the colonnade of masks (ambush), the temple steps (the treasury, a vault, a side room off them), west along the cloister (the shortcut), down the well stair and east again UNDER the colonnade through the undercroft (dark) to the old shrine (safe room, healer). From the shrine a vine door leads to the WING: the strangler's climb thirty up, the high canopy (the hard parkour) and the high sanctum, where on some runs the PRIZE waits (Hakamo-o, from band 4 Zarude) and a balcony hides the seed idol. On one heal: the FALLEN COURT, the second crossroads: the glyph door (a puzzle) or round through the root crawl (dark, longer). The Tangle (mini-boss), the canopy closing over the hall (the set piece) and the altar (the Gardener). Fights never meet: a non-fight room stands between any two on every route

dungeons.design: The Burned Tower of the old story, sunk into the nether wastes (NETHER_ENCOUNTERS.md 3.1; the roster's story). THE YARD: the ash gate, the cinder yard where the slugs and coal imps nest (optional), a pilgrims' stair south to the ash bowl (a wishing well) and the bait cellar. THE TOWER: the ringers' loft (the peal rung back, a puzzle), the keepers' hall (the Tower Keeper and the Bell Ringer), the burned stacks (a maze), the slag heap (the quartz and gold seam, a cracked face). THE CHARRED NAVE is a three-way crossroads, every way in sight from the bell plate: the ringers' walk (lit, fast, it gives way behind you), the undercroft (dark and long) or the quench stair (down to the cistern valves, a puzzle); all three meet round THE FALLEN BELL (a mini-boss sleeping against it, a cracked face, the abbot's strongroom off its east wall: a bank vault whose code is scratched in three rooms on the way). Down the bell pit and back west UNDER the fallen bell: the soot drift, the ash cloister, the vigil room (the healer, a shortcut back to the soot drift), the smoke way. THE RAIN COURT is the second crossroads: the rafters (lit, the long parkour, six sections) or the bell cellar (dark, signed shut, OPTIONAL: the cellar beams' hard parkour, the ash ring with a balcony relic and the hidden prize, a road back up). Both come out in the choir hall (the Ashen Choir's two cantors step out of the smoke), then the tower fall (the floor gives way behind you) and the belfry (the Bell Warden, two stages, a full heal between)

dungeons.design: NEW-OSSUARY (2026-10-11), the roster's Soul Ossuary (data/dungeon_prize_roster.json soul_ossuary) on the soul valley theme. The OUTER VALLEY: the rib maze, the soul cradle (a nest; the bone bed's fossil dig and the soul well with the offering cairn open off it as side rooms), north and up the ash stair, the ridge of ribs (the main parkour, six sections). The PILGRIMS' CROSSING is a three-way crossroads, every way in sight from its middle: the bonepickers' trail east (dark, a fight: their camp, with the cracked stash), the spine bridge north (lit, fast, a collapse that costs a fall) or the old riverbed south (safe and long); all three meet in the quartz scar (resources). The OSSUARY: the nave (an ambush of two sextons), the charnel porch (the reliquary vault, a bank vault whose code is chalked in the cradle, the scar and the nave, opens off its east wall), west along the bone cloister (the shortcut into the nave), down the charnel stair and east again UNDER the nave through the catacomb (dark, a cracked niche with the named skull) to the bone chapel (safe room, healer). From the chapel a bone door leads to the WING: the skull stair thirty up, the high ribs (the hard parkour) and the reliquary, where from band 5 on some runs the PRIZE waits (the roster's pool) and a balcony hides the keeper's lamp. On one heal: the CHARNEL COURT, the second crossroads: the bone seal (a puzzle) or round through the crypt (dark, longer). The warden's hall (a mini-boss rolled from the band's pool), the last vigil (lights out) and the ossuary (the Keeper: two crews, a full heal between, Blacephalon last). Fights never meet: a non-fight room stands between any two on every route. VARIETY per run: every trainer rotates between two teams a band (team_pool_by_band), the warden is one of two or three species a band (species_pool_by_band), the Keeper has an alternate crew list a band (teams_alt_by_band)

dungeons.design: The Moth Cathedral (unit NEW-MOTH, 2026-10-11): a cathedral the crimson forest grew from its own stems round the roost of a sun-moth, kept by the Chandlers, who keep the shroomlights burning so the moths come. The route CLIMBS through it: the narthex, the stem aisle (a maze of wart and hyphae), the Chandlers' rail (a stand of two, a votive font off it), the bell stair up into the rafters (the main parkour, six sections), the CROSSING, three ways in sight from its middle: the choir loft's catwalk (lit, fast, it falls behind you), the Sexton's walk (dark, a fight in the dark of the charnel aisle) or the font stair down through the baptistry (flooded, long and safe); all three meet in the chapter house (the seam of quartz and gold, the tithe vault off it). Then the moth gallery (an ambush of two acolytes), the sacristy (the cocoonery off it), WEST along the cloister (the shortcut back into the gallery), UP the spiral stair and EAST again ABOVE the gallery through the triforium, where the moths roost (a nest), to the lady chapel (the heal). From the chapel the WING goes DOWN thirty into the crypt: the charnel road, the ossuary pits (the hard parkour) and the reliquary, where on some runs the PRIZE sleeps (Victini; Slither Wing and Iron Moth once their models reach the players) and a balcony hides the sun-moth's scale. On one heal: the AMBULATORY, the second crossroads: the rose window (a puzzle) or the ash walk (dark, longer); the Great Moth (mini-boss), the nave going dark as the moths smother the lights (the set piece) and the sanctuary (the High Chandler, two stages, a full heal between). Fights never meet: a non-fight room stands between any two on every route
